w: In the evening assembly, a drama, 'Naiya Par', showed how Bhagatji Maharaj through his powers defused a life-threatening storm at sea and thus saved Ganpatbhai of Bharuch and Jethabhai Patel of Pij. Swamishri, in his blessings, appreciated the drama and said, "If one has refuge in God and His Sadhu then whatever difficulty arises, God protects in some way. But one must have faith and trust… Life in this world is like a camel ride. It is also compared with the vast ocean wherein one experiences both happiness and misery…"
Today's Gunatit Din was dedicated to the life and works of Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami.

The evening assembly was centered around Gunatitanand Swami's Yash Gatha. Sadhus sang one verse depicting Gunatitanand Swami's glory, after which this verse was explained by a drama, a speech or a presentation.

Swamishri also described Gunatitanand Swami's qualities in his blessings to the assembly, narrating various incidents, such as, Gunatitanand Swami's transformation of the notorious Munjo Suru. He stressed the fact that Bhagwan Swaminarayan came on earth together with his divine abode in the form of Gunatitanand Swami.

ds.t: "The great one's wish is our wish"
w: Upendra and Krishnamurti phoned from London.

Upendra said, "Today we commemorated the twenty fifth anniversary of the Suvarna Tula (weighing against gold) celebrated in London. I still remember exactly the gesture you made with your hand at the end."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said laughingly, "Since you remember it, your work is done."
Upendra said, "You always say that everything happens through the wish of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. So today, please tell us, what is your wish?"
Swamishri said, "The wish of the great one is our wish. We have to obey his commands and do bhajan."

A fax had come from Kothari Dharmakirti Swami of Junagadh. In it he had written the details: "Haribhai Mehta is a lifelong volunteer here. He has been serving since 1993. Earlier he was the pujari at the Hari Mandir. Now he serves at the Nilkanth Varni Abhishek Mandapam. Every morning he walks 4 kilometres to reach the mandir by 6:00. He is 85 years old. He bathes in cold water."
After reading this much, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Tell him that he should now bathe in hot water." Then he said again, "If cold water does not trouble him, let him bathe in cold water."
In saying this, the feeling of care for a devoted devotee that overflowed in Swamishri's advice was truly worth seeing.

ds.t: A big envelope for a small letter
w: A large envelope marked Priority Mail had come from America. Inside the envelope was just a loose letter of two pages. Seeing this letter, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "The letter is small, and look how big an envelope he has used!"
Showing the postage slip on the envelope, Dharmacharan Swami said, "It has cost about 14 dollars to send these two pages."
Swamishri said, "Why spend so much for such a small letter? What was the need? Could it not have been sent some other way?"

On the plane from Los Angeles to Houston.
The cardiac (heart) surgeon Dr Kirit, who had joined today's journey, was also there. Atmaswarupdas Swami asked him, "As a cardiac surgeon, what is your advice to Mahant Swami Maharaj?"
He said, "Nothing, because there are three main things to watch."
Diet: in this, Swamishri is absolutely perfect. He eats the right food in the right amount.
Exercise: Swamishri also walks regularly and so on, and
Stress: Swamishri immediately made a zero with his hand and said, "Zero."
Vivekmurtidas Swami asked, "Do you never feel stress (tension or worry)?"
Swamishri clearly said "No."
"How?"
"Bhagwan is the doer. It is Maharaj who does everything! And he does it well," said Swamishri, reinforcing the understanding of who the doer is.

Vivekmurtidas Swami put forward his dilemma: "But if we have such an understanding, we could never say anything to anyone! If something wrong is happening, don't we have to say it as part of our responsibility?"
"For responsibility you have to say it, but do not frighten anyone," said Swamishri.
Swamishri taught the key to staying free of stress, and discretion, and everything, very well.
